newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up on Pakistan tender, Japan buy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up on Pakistan tender, Japan buy.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed higher on prospects for a large sale of U.S. wheat to Pakistan and on news Japan this week bought 120,000 tonnes U.S. wheat.
"Japan bought wheat last night and there was a lack of fund selling," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Transportation problems in Canada led to ideas that Asian demand for U.S. wheat may increase and the market took note of this week's sale to Japan.
Also, there is evidence Australia is booked up on wheat sales which could lead to U.S. deals with Pakistan.
"There's port congestion in Australia. They've got a big export program going on," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
U.S. exporters and traders Thursday said the U.S. could get the lion's share of this weekend's expanded Pakistani wheat tender.
"It will be U.S. and for 450,000 tonnes," a trader said.
Wheat closed one to two cents higher, with March up 1-3/4 at $3.59 and July ended one cent higher at $3.43 per bushel.

"Pakistan upped the quantity of wheat over the weekend and we're the only ones who can sell it because everyone else is booked up," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.
Officials in Islamabad early Thursday said Pakistan plans to buy up to 600,000 tonnes of wheat by April to complete its import target of 2.4 million tonnes in fiscal 1996-97 (July-June).
Support also came from a wheat export sales number near the high end of expectations.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. net export sales of wheat for the week ended February 6 totaled 298,700 tonnes. The trade was expecting 200,000 to 300,000 tonnes.
There also was widespread talk early Thursday that Iraq bought from 25,000 to 95,000 tonnes of wheat from the U.S.
"We got strength from what appeared to be big commercial buying yesterday during the fund long liquidation and Iraq bought U.S. wheat overnight," Searcy said.

Roughly 10 to 12 commission houses and funds each bought from 0.5 million to 1.0 million bushels of March, traders said. Rosenthal Collins sold two million bushels of March and Term Commodities sold 1.2 million March, traders said.
Bull spreading boosted the March contract relative to other months. FIMAT Futures did 1.4 million bushels of March/July and Cargill Inc did 1.3 million bushels of March/May, traders said.

Technicians early Thursday cited first support in the March at $3.53-1/2 and second support at $3.45-1/2. The session low for March was $3.57. First resistance for March was at $3.61-1/2 and second resistance was $3.69-1/2. The session high for March was $3.63.

Chart followers cited a short term barometer for the March as nearing neutral territory with the nine day relative strength index (RSI) closing at 40 percent. The trade views a market as oversold with an RSI of 30 or less and overbought at 70 or more.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 17,000 contracts, below the 22,766 traded Wednesday.
In wheat options, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 400 May $3.70 calls at 7-1/2 cents and Prudential Securities bought 100 March $3.50 puts at 1-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,500 contracts, below the 4,033 traded Wednesday.
